sources.entry: OvenMediaEngine - Streaming Server with Sub-Second Latency. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 C++/Docker

summary.one_liner: OvenMediaEngine is a C++ live streaming server that ingests streams over WebRTC, SRT, RTMP, RTSP and MPEG-2 TS and delivers them to viewers with sub-second latency via LLHLS and WebRTC.
summary.what_it_does: OvenMediaEngine (OME) ingests live streams over WebRTC, WHIP, SRT, RTMP, E-RTMP, RTSP, OVT and MPEG-2 TS/UDP. It includes an embedded live transcoder that encodes to ABR (VP8, H.264, H.265, AV1, Opus, AAC) and serves viewers over Low Latency HLS and WebRTC, with a legacy HLS v3 output and SRT output as well. The README also lists an embedded WebRTC signalling server, an embedded TURN server, DVR/live rewind, DRM (Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady), WebVTT subtitles, file recording, and push re-streaming to SRT, RTMP and MPEG-2 TS. Access control is handled through admission webhooks and signed policies, and a REST API and clustering (origin-edge structure) are provided. The README claims support for hundreds of thousands of viewers.
use_cases: live video streaming to large audiences
re-streaming RTMP or SRT input to other destinations
adaptive bitrate live streaming with LLHLS
how_to_run: Optional: add -v ome-origin-conf:/opt/ovenmediaengine/bin/origin_conf -v ome-edge-conf:/opt/ovenmediaengine/bin/edge_conf to persist configuration files
Building from source requires libstdc++ 10 or newer (see README for supported platforms)
notable: Sub-second latency streaming over both WebRTC and LLHLS from one server
Embedded live transcoder producing ABR outputs without a separate transcoding service
Accepts many ingest protocols including WebRTC/WHIP, SRT, RTMP, RTSP and MPEG-2 TS
Origin-edge clustering plus admission webhooks and signed policies for access control
Companion projects OvenPlayer and OvenLiveKit for playback and browser-based encoding
caveats: Building from source needs libstdc++ 10 or newer; older distributions such as Ubuntu 18.04/20.04 and RHEL 8 must use the Docker image
Hardware H.265 transcoding is listed as hardware only; commercial licensing is available by contacting the maintainers for non-AGPL use
